The Switzerland-based firm is the third largest Anchor Coca-Cola bottler in the world Coca-Cola HBC shares rose for more than 9% during morning negotiation By Harry Wise
Updated: 16:35 GMT, February 13, 2025
Coca-Cola HBC Share He reached a higher record on Thursday after the bottling firm challenged the winds against it to achieve increasing profits.
The shares of the company based in Switzerland, the third largest coca-cool anchor bottling to be quoted.
The firm reported that its comparable net earnings grew by 8.5 percent to € 828.8 million last year, while operational profits increased by almost a quarter to € 1.2 billion.
This was despite the important adverse impacts of the devaluation of the Nigerian Naira, the Russian ruble and the Egyptian Libra coins.
Net sales revenue increased 5.6 percent to € 10.75 billion, partly due to price increases and the deployment of Finland Vodka, which Coca-Cola HBC bought in 2023 the owner of Jack Daniels, Brown-Forman .
The majority of rotation growth came from developing markets, which cover much of Eastern Europe, where it increased by 14.2 percent to € 2.4 billion thanks to the increase in sprite volumes, Coke Zero and Monster Energy

However, the company also enjoyed a healthy result in markets established as Greece in the back of a booming tourism market, and the percentage volume expansion of two digits in coffee and energy drinks.
Zoran Bogdanovic, executive director of Coca-Cola HBC, said: “2024 showed that we can achieve consistently strong financial performance even in a variety of market conditions.”
He added: “While we hope that the macroeconomic and geopolitical environment remains challenging, in the next year, we are sure that our portfolio, capacities and people will allow us to advance against our medium -term growth goals.”
On an organic basis, Coca-Cola HBC anticipates that income increases by 6 to 8 percent by 2025 and operational profits increase from 7 to 11 percent.
Coca-Cola, which has a 21 percent participation in HBC, warned Wednesday that it could sell more drinks in plastic bottles if their aluminum cans become more expensive due to the tariffs of the president of the United States, Donald Trump.
Trump announced an import tax of 25 percent throughout the steel and aluminum that enters the US. UU. Earlier this week under measures to increase national manufacturing.
The company has been the world’s largest plastic contaminator for six years, according to the plastic free campaign organization.
However, while companies expect to see additional cost pressures of the rates, Zoran Bogdanovic said that any effect on the prices of the basic products would be “irrelevant” for the bottler.
Coca-Cola HBC sells dozens of brands ranging from Schweppes to Fanta, Campari, Powerade and Costa Coffee to customers in 29 countries.
